RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

Requested Service: ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-18
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-14

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888), as described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-18. The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I respectfully disagree, and I am submitting this appeal along with supporting clinical documentation for reconsideration.

**Background on the applicable criteria**

I understand that prior authorization for knee surgery under my Harvard Pilgrim Health Care plan is administered through Evolent (formerly National Imaging Associates), and that Evolent publishes ACL-reconstruction medical-necessity criteria as part of its "Knee Arthroscopy" guideline. A copy of Evolent's own published clinical tip sheet for this guideline (cited there as guideline "Evolent_CG-316") states the following criteria for ACL reconstruction:

"ACL reconstruction requests do not require non-operative treatment provided the following criteria are met: Knee instability (as defined subjectively as 'giving way', 'giving out', 'buckling', two-fist sign) with clinical findings of instability: Lachman's 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B, 3A, 3B, Anterior Drawer, Pivot Shift test, or instrumented (KT-1000 or KT-2000) laxity of greater than 3 mm side-side difference; MRI results confirm complete ACL tear; Member has no evidence of severe arthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4 [see grading appendix]) on weight-bearing x-rays."

I have not been able to independently confirm that this is the exact version, section number, or effective date of the criteria applied to my specific request on 2026-08-18. I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that Harvard Pilgrim and/or Evolent provide me and my surgeon with the precise document (title, version/effective date, and section) that was relied upon in issuing this denial, as I am entitled to receive the specific medical necessity criteria used in my adverse determination.

**Why my clinical record satisfies the quoted criteria**

Based on the criteria quoted above, my clinical record demonstrates:

1. **Knee instability, subjectively reported and objectively confirmed on examination.** I have experienced recurrent instability with pivoting and have given way twice on stairs — this is precisely the type of subjective instability ("giving way") referenced in the criteria. My exam also documented positive provocative testing on the affected side, consistent with the clinical instability findings (e.g., Lachman, Anterior Drawer, Pivot Shift) that the criteria list as qualifying findings. [If a specific named test (Lachman/Anterior Drawer/Pivot Shift) and its grade was recorded in Dr. Marchetti's exam note, please cite that grade here.]

2. **MRI results confirm a complete ACL tear.** My MRI of 2026-06-11 documented a "complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with bone bruise pattern" — this directly and unambiguously satisfies the criterion requiring "MRI results confirm complete ACL tear." This finding was part of the imaging packet submitted with the original prior authorization request, and it is not clear how the denial concluded that "imaging findings... do not support medical necessity" when the MRI report itself confirms a complete ACL tear.

3. **No evidence of severe arthritis.** My MRI report also noted intact menisci and no significant arthritis. This is consistent with the criterion requiring the absence of severe (Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) arthritis. [If weight-bearing knee x-rays with a specific Kellgren-Lawrence grade were obtained and are not already in the file, please advise if these are needed, and I will ask Dr. Marchetti's office to submit them; my available imaging shows no significant arthritic change.]

Taken together, these three elements — subjective and clinical instability, MRI-confirmed complete ACL tear, and absence of severe arthritis — match, point for point, the criteria quoted above for ACL reconstruction.

**Additional supporting history (beyond what the quoted criteria require)**

The quoted criteria state that "ACL reconstruction requests do not require non-operative treatment" once the above findings are met. Even though conservative treatment was not required for approval, I completed an extensive course of conservative care without adequate relief, which further supports the medical necessity of surgery:

- 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy for range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, with bracing, from 2026-04-19 to 2026-07-12 (20 visits completed), as documented in my physical therapy discharge note;
- 6 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief;
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-09 that provided only 3 weeks of partial relief;
- 12 months of progressive knee pain unrelieved by rest, with function limited by pain on range of motion.

I have no active infection, no untreated substance use disorder, and a BMI of 29; I am a non-smoker. There is no medical contraindication to surgery, and my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has recommended ACL reconstruction based on this clinical picture.

**Requested action**

I ask that Harvard Pilgrim/Evolent:

1. Reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 29888 (ACL reconstruction) as requested by Dr. Marchetti;
2. Provide, in writing, the specific medical necessity guideline document (title, guideline number, and effective/revision date) that was actually applied to my case, if different from the Evolent Knee Arthroscopy guideline criteria quoted above; and
3. If further clinical information or a peer-to-peer conversation between Dr. Marchetti and the reviewing physician would assist in this reconsideration, please contact Dr. Marchetti's office at [surgeon office phone number] to arrange this.

Enclosed with this appeal are copies of:
- The physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-19 to 2026-07-12);
- The MRI report dated 2026-06-11;
- Office visit/exam notes documenting instability and provocative testing findings;
- [Any additional records the provider's office wishes to include, e.g., weight-bearing x-rays if obtained.]

I understand that I have the right to a full and fair review of this appeal, and, if the denial is upheld, the right to pursue external review through the Massachusetts Health Policy Commission's Office of Patient Protection (50 Milk Street, 8th Floor, Boston, MA 02109; 1-800-436-7757). I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day deadline stated in your notice (by 2027-02-14).

Please contact me at [phone number] or [email address] if you need any additional information. Thank you for your prompt reconsideration of this matter.

Sincerely,

_____________________________
Cameron Jennings
